articles.title: Woody Harrelson Turned Down Haymitch Offer Twice: I Didn’t ‘Think There Was Enough to Do’ in ‘The Hunger Games’
articles.summary: While a certain generation might associate Woody Harrelson most with his role as Haymitch Abernathy in the billion-dollar “Hunger Games” franchise, the actor has admitted he needed convincing to sign on for the dystopian film.
body: “Turned it down?” asked Zada. “Yeah, it’s stupid,” responded Harrelson. “I thought it was good, I read the books, really good, but I just don’t think there’s enough to do. I don’t know if there’s enough to do. It’s an arbitrary, odd way of assessing it.”

Released in 2012, Ross directed the first “Hunger Games” film, while Francis Lawrence went on to direct “Catching Fire,” “Mockingjay – Part 1,” “Mockingjay – Part 2,” “The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes” and “Sunrise on the Reaping.” The recently released prequel takes place 25 years before the original “Hunger Games” series and follows the origin story of Abernathy as he’s forced to compete in the second Quarter Quell. McKenna Grace, Ralph Fiennes, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning and more also star.

In addition to Harrelson, who returned for the film, original cast members Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson also made small appearances. On an episode of “Call Her Daddy,” Lawrence told host Alex Cooper it was “unbelievable” to return as Katniss. “It was so crazy. It was the same crew. It was the same AD, who I’ve worked with a million times because I love him. And with Josh [Hutcherson] and Woody [Harrelson] … it was so emotional.”

articles.title: Marathi Crime Drama ‘Hurda – That Tight Green Top’ Puts a Journalist’s Masculinity Under the Microscope at WAVES Film Bazaar
articles.summary: Apurv Gaikwad is presnting his debut feature “Hurda – That Tight Green Top,” a Marathi-language crime drama adapted from Atharva Pandit’s novel, to the Co-Production Market at WAVES Film Bazaar.
body: Gaikwad says he was drawn to the story because he “was fascinated by its polyphonic narrative, the way multiple characters coexist, each with their own distinct voice.” He adds, “Even months after reading the novel, there was one particular aspect of it that refused to leave me – the protagonist, Chitranshu.”

“It is as much a mystery as it is a character study and an exploration of the society we live in. While the audience may find the answers they initially seek, I hope they leave the film with an entirely different set of questions,” says Gaikwad, who previously made the short mockumentary “The Last Auteur.”

Gaikwad hopes to challenge the binary understanding of masculinity and “the comfortable distinction we make between good men and bad men. I hope the film encourages audiences to question their own prejudices and examine how caste, gender and social hierarchies shape their understanding of truth, justice and morality,” he says.

articles.title: Bela Bajaria Reflects on Her Netflix Experience and Says ‘Stay Tuned’ at International Emmy Awards
articles.summary: Former Netflix executive Bela Bajaria put the emphasis on her belief in the transformative power of storytelling while accepting the Founders Award Monday night at the International Emmy Awards in New York.
body: In a nod to this week’s Thanksgiving holiday, Bajaria opened by expressing her gratitude for the opportunities she’s been afforded since her family relocated to Southern California in the late 1970s, when she was in grade school.

“Gratitude isn’t passive or soft. It’s earned. Gratitude is strength in knowing nothing is guaranteed, and nothing can be taken for granted. Gratitude is the appreciation for both struggle and success, and sharing the journey with others,” Bajaria told the crowd.

During most of the past decade, Bajaria was focused on building out Netflix’s local-language TV content operation at a scale never before seen in the industry. The experience was profound as the regional teams set off on a search for new creative voices.
Bajaria indicated pride in the legacy of her role having greatly expanded the global village of television during her tenure at Netflix.

articles.title: King Charles and Elton John pay tribute to Australian music legend Molly Meldrum
articles.summary: The promoter and broadcaster helped define the music tastes of Australians for decades.
body: King Charles and Elton John have paid tribute to Australian music industry legend Molly Meldrum, who died aged 83 after a long illness.
Meldrum's family said he "passed away peacefully" at a hospital in Melbourne in the early hours of Monday morning.
The music promoter and broadcaster, born Ian Alexander Meldrum, helped define the nation's music tastes for decades, championing local artists like INXS and Kylie Minogue and global acts like Abba.
Known for his chaotic demeanour and trademark Stetson hat, he interviewed an array of stars, with the king on Monday calling him "a true giant of the music industry".

articles.title: Shanghai Golden Goblet Winner Ridham Janve Stages a Goan Village Death Watch in ‘Goodbye Mr D’Mello’ at WAVES Film Bazaar
articles.summary: Ridham Janve, whose “Hunter’s Moon” won the Golden Goblet Award for best screenplay at the Shanghai International Film Festival this year, is bringing “Goodbye Mr D’Mello,” a dark comedy set in a Goan village, to the Co-Production Market at WAVES Film Bazaar.
body: “Living in Goa, I have been fascinated by the peculiarities of its social life, its people, humor and contradictions,” says Janve, who developed the screenplay with Goan journalist and writer Mayabhushan Nagvenkar. “There is also something fascinating about how traditional village gossip has found new life through WhatsApp and social media. It is also both amusing and disturbing about how easily another person’s private life can become a public spectacle.”
Janve’s debut feature, “The Gold-Laden Sheep and the Sacred Mountain,” premiered at the International Film Festival Rotterdam (IFFR). His second, “Hunter’s Moon,” premiered in Shanghai.

The film is being produced by Sharib Khan and Vikas Kumar through Khan & Kumar Media, alongside Nagvenkar through Mountain Motion Pictures, Janve’s production company. This is the producers’ second collaboration with Janve, following “Hunter’s Moon.”

articles.summary: Other top winners include 'División Palermo' for best comedy, best actor Bobby Schofield for 'Unforgivable' and best actress Mona Mina Leon for 'Holy Sh!t.'
body: The International Emmy Awards, the global version of the U.S. TV honors, were handed out in New York Monday night.

The top prize of best drama went to French foodie-themed period series Carême from Apple TV. The series beat out Steven Knight’s Hulu boxing drama A Thousand Blows; Prime Video’s Argentine political drama Menem; and underdog sports drama Real Kashmir Football Club from Indian pay-TV group Sony LIV.

Netflix went into the 54th International Emmys the clear frontrunner with nine nominations, including all four best comedy noms — for the Rowan Atkinson slapstick series Man vs. Baby; the Spanish sitcom Old Dog, New Tricks; Argentine satire División Palermo; and Vir Das: Fool Volume, the latest comedy special from the Indian stand-up star. División Palermo won the award.
Still that prize was the only one that went to a program from the streamer.

articles.title: US rapper postpones two arena shows after Manchester evacuation
articles.summary: Don Toliver's show on Sunday was evacuated after an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd.
body: Toliver was due to play The O2 on Monday and Wembley Arena on Tuesday, but Live Nation said his "stage and production equipment remains in Manchester and cannot be moved in time".
One person was taken to hospital and 89 people showed "symptoms believed to be linked to the exposure" after Sunday's Co-op Live arena show, police said.
Fans described "distressing scenes" with people "choking", "screaming" and "coughing up blood" because of the effects of a substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas.
The Wembley show has been rescheduled to 14 December, while Monday night's O2 gig has been moved to 15 December.

articles.title: The Naruto Movie Sounds Like It Could Be Better Than We Ever Imagined
articles.summary: Based on recent casting-related developments and other factors, things are looking very promising for the live-action Naruto movie adaptation.
body: Fresh off making the best "Spider-Man" movie in about a decade with "Brand New Day," director Destin Daniel Cretton is plunging into the Land of Fire and ninjas, adapting Masashi Kishimoto's manga/worldwide phenomenon "Naruto" into a live-action film, two years after it was first announced. Translating a battle shonen manga/anime into live-action carries negative associations of past, failed attempts. Why bother moving a story designed to stretch reality's limits to a medium that's inherently more confining than a hand-drawn one? Will "Naruto" break this curse? It has a huge stage to do so, and the early steps look promising.

Deadline has reported that actor Hiroyuki Sanada ("Shogun," "John Wick: Chapter 4") is in negotiations to star in "Naruto" as Hiruzen Sarutobi, the Third Hokage and leader of Naruto's ninja village, Konohagakure. Sanada is the second major actor rumored to be joining "Naruto," after reports in August that Charles Melton had been approached to play Kakashi Hatake, Naruto's masked sensei.

articles.title: New ‘Hunger Games’ Movie on the Way? Lionsgate Film Chief Shares Latest on Franchise’s Future
articles.summary: Adam Fogelson tells The Hollywood Reporter that his team hopes to connect soon with author Suzanne Collins about a new project: "I will sit patiently and wait for that phone call."
body: The Hunger Games franchise has whetted appetites for more films, given the success of its latest title.

During a conversation with The Hollywood Reporter to celebrate the success of Sunrise on the Reaping, Lionsgate Motion Picture Group chair Adam Fogelson emphasizes that the studio would love to collaborate again with Collins on another project in the franchise. Director Francis Lawrence ‘s latest movie stars Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy, portrayed in the first four films by Woody Harrelson. The $150 million-budgeted feature is set 24 years before the events of Collins’ original 2008 book.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping had a far bigger impact at the box office than the 2023 prequel film The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, which starred Tom Blyth, Rachel Zegler and Hunter Schafer. Centering on the backstory for villainous President Snow — portrayed in the new movie by Ralph Fiennes — Songbirds and Snakes opened to $44 million domestically before ending its run with $166.4 million domestically and a global sum of $361.8 million.

articles.title: Britain's Got Talent winner almost missed audition due to Carphone Warehouse shift
articles.summary: Tenor Paul Potts would have missed his big chance if a colleague didn't work his Saturday shift.
body: Britain's Got Talent winner Paul Potts said he nearly missed his life-changing audition on the show because he had been unable to get time off from his job managing a phone shop.

The tenor shot to fame in 2007 after performing Nessun Dorma on the ITV talent show, but had unsuccessfully tried to change the date of his performance because of his shift at Port Talbot's Carphone Warehouse.
"It was only thanks to a colleague who normally didn't work Saturdays that came into cover me – otherwise I wouldn't have been there," he said.
He has since released six albums, reached the final of America's Got Talent: The Champions and inspired the Hollywood film One Chance.

articles.title: ‘GTA 6’ Boss Strauss Zelnick Among First Raft of SXSW London 2027 Speakers
articles.summary: The upcoming installment — built around the theme "The Power of Human Potential" — has also enlisted former DeepMind creative lead Jon Steinback and president of Genomics Limited David Thornton.
body: Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick, the man behind Grand Theft Auto VI, is among the first raft of speakers confirmed for next year’s SXSW London.

The conference is set to return to Shoreditch, east London, for its third year from May 24-29, where Zelnick will take to the stage to talk about building one of the world’s biggest entertainment franchises (sales for the latest release have already out-grossed Christopher Nolan’s box office behemoth The Odyssey ).
Elsewhere, David Thornton, president of Genomics Limited, will explore how rapid analysis of large-scale genetic and genomic information will empower us to predict disease risks and improve medicine.

Ilyas Khan, who founded Cambridge Quantum and was the founding CEO of Quantinuum, is also on board to discuss the convergence of AI and quantum computing. His appearance follows Quantinuum’s $1.68bn Nasdaq listing in June 2026, the largest traditional IPO yet for a pure-play quantum computing company.
